_why: Write-edge ratchet baseline (2026-08-01). CI sat red 30 days because every gate was absolute over a dirty tree: red became the normal state, so a NEW red carried no information and nobody looked. These counts make green achievable TODAY at the current debt level while making the debt monotonically non-increasing. Debt may fall or hold; it may never rise without editing this file in the same commit, which turns a silent increase into a recorded decision.
_how_to_pay_down: Fix violations, re-run scripts/githooks/pre_commit.py guardrail_counts(), and LOWER the number here in the same commit. Never raise it to make a commit pass -- that is the rubber stamp this replaces.

_check_boundaries_3: 2026-08-14 claude (W162): PAID DOWN 4 -> 3. The redis-family rule fired for the first time in W161 (it had been failing open on an import that could never succeed) and surfaced four unregistered families. One is now classified: bus.py:971's {ns}:seat_seen -- the T108 dual-delivery dedupe mark -- added to EPHEMERAL_PREFIXES, which is its honest home because the family exists to expire (SET NX EX 1200). The finding underneath it was a SPELLING FORK: the roster already held '*:seatseen:*' (seat PRESENCE, 19 live keys) and bus.py writes 'seat_seen' (the dedupe mark, 0 live keys because of the 20-minute TTL). One underscore, two families, and registering one never covered the other. THE REMAINING 3 ARE DELIBERATE: role_queue.py's {ns}:role, {ns}:rolefence, {ns}:rolegen carry no TTL, have zero live keys, sit in a module check_wiring lists as built-ahead with no production consumer, and that file is MODIFIED in prod's tree by another seat right now. Classifying the key families of a module someone else is still writing is guessing on their behalf, and a wrong call is worse than an unregistered one -- it would tell the heal machinery their state is expendable. tests/test_w162 pins the omission so it reads as a decision. PAY DOWN: whoever lands role_queue classifies its three and lowers this to 0.
_check_boundaries_4: 2026-08-14 claude (W161): this is a MEASUREMENT change, not a debt increase, and it is the one case the 'never raise it to make a commit pass' rule does not cover -- so it is spelled out rather than assumed. check_boundaries' redis-family rule imports core.comm.packet_spec and its own docstring says 'Fail-open on import error'. The repo root was never on sys.path when the checker ran as a script (python puts the SCRIPT's dir on sys.path[0], not the cwd), so that import ALWAYS failed, the rule ALWAYS returned an empty set, and it has therefore never once fired. W161 put the root on sys.path while fixing the checker's hardcoded ROOT, and the rule ran for the first time: 4 unregistered redis families surfaced -- bus.py {ns}:seat_seen, role_queue.py {ns}:role, {ns}:rolefence, {ns}:rolegen. All four PRE-DATE this session and none are in a file this arc touched. Raising the number is what makes them countable and therefore payable; leaving it at 0 would mean the rule goes back to being decorative. PAY THIS DOWN by registering the four families in packet_spec (ephemeral roster or DURABLE_FAMILIES) and lowering this to 0 -- it is a real, small, owned task for the core/comm lane, not permanent debt.
